claim: Multi-agent orchestration is defined by four control decisions: which agent runs when (control flow), what each agent gets to see (state), how outputs are combined (combination), and when the run stops (termination).
stance_target: definitional framework for multi-agent orchestration systems
scope_conditions: general multi-agent orchestration, Swarms API framing, 2026
quoted_support: Multi-agent orchestration is the control layer around a group of LLM agents. It makes four decisions: which agent runs when, what each agent gets to see, how their outputs are combined, and when the run stops.

claim: In the Swarms API, every agent listed in a swarm config is billed a flat per-agent fee even if a router-based pattern never calls that agent.
stance_target: cost-optimization pitfall of router/hierarchical patterns where unused agents still incur fixed cost
quoted_support: Agents the router does not pick never run, so they add no tokens, though each one listed still counts toward the per-agent fee covered in the cost section below.

claim: The recommended failure-handling pattern for an orchestrated multi-agent run is to gate any swarm's output through a judge pattern (e.g. CouncilAsAJudge) before it ships, rather than trusting the primary swarm's output directly.
stance_target: necessity of a dedicated verification/judge layer as adversarial review before output is trusted
quoted_support: For other patterns, add a gate: the docs suggest generating a response with one swarm call, then sending the original task plus that response through CouncilAsAJudge.

claim: Swarm API loop limits (max_loops) default to 1 and are capped at 50 at the swarm level, with per-agent max_loops ranging 1-50 or 'auto' to let the agent decide when it is done.
stance_target: concrete bounding mechanism against runaway/idle agent loops
quoted_support: The swarm-level max_loops defaults to 1 and is capped at 50. ... Each agent has its own max_loops as well, an integer from 1 to 50 or "auto" to let the agent decide when it is done.

claim: On failure responses, the correct retry policy is to back off on HTTP 429 and 500 with Retry-After-respecting backoff, but to fail immediately on 401, 402, 403, or 422 because those error codes will not change on retry.
stance_target: correct client-side failure-handling design for agent API orchestration layers
quoted_support: back off on 429 using the Retry-After header and retry 500 with backoff. A 401 (bad key), 402 (credit balance too low), 403 (premium-only model or endpoint) or 422 (invalid request) will fail the same way on a second try, so raise those immediately.

claim: Shared-transcript patterns (GroupChat, RoundRobin) are recommended to be limited to small rosters because each new turn reads the full growing history, so input-token cost increases with every turn.
stance_target: cost/context-growth tradeoff of conversational multi-agent orchestration patterns
quoted_support: Shared transcripts make agents responsive to each other. They also grow with every turn, so each new turn reads more input tokens than the one before. The docs recommend small rosters for both: three to six agents for GroupChat and three to five for RoundRobin.
